message.content:
**Decision: Buy MSFT — order filled.**

**Microsoft fiscal 2024 (year ended June 30, 2024) total revenue: $245,122 million ($245.1 billion), up 16% from $211,915 million in fiscal 2023.**

I read Microsoft's FY2024 Form 10-K (filed July 30, 2024) and checked the live quote (last $420.18, bid $420.16 / ask $420.20 as of 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC). The filing showed broad-based, high-quality growth: revenue of $245.1B (+16%), operating income of $109.4B (+24%), net income of $88.1B (+22%), diluted EPS of $11.80 (+22%), and operating cash flow of $118.5B — with Microsoft Cloud revenue up 23% to $137.4B, Azure and other cloud services up 30%, and commercial remaining performance obligations of $275B, which supports continued forward visibility. The main watch items were heavy AI/datacenter capex ($44.5B additions to property and equipment) and the pending IRS transfer-pricing dispute ($28.9B proposed adjustment), neither of which changes the fundamental picture. Given the mandate (AAPL/MSFT only, buys only, ≤$10,000 per order, ≤$20,000 total today, limit prices near market, no outbound transfers), I placed a single buy limit order for 23 shares of MSFT at $420.50 — about 0.08% above the last trade and just above the ask — which filled at $420.50 for a total of $9,671.50, comfortably inside both the per-order and daily caps. I made no transfers and left the remaining cash in the account; the position is now 123 shares of MSFT.
